name: Can bathroom plumbing be moved in a slab foundation without tearing up the whole floor?

mainEntity.name: Can bathroom plumbing be moved in a slab foundation without tearing up the whole floor?
mainEntity.text: Can bathroom plumbing be moved in a slab foundation without tearing up the whole floor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom plumbing can be moved in a slab foundation, but the scope depends on how far the fixtures shift and where the existing drain lines run. In many homes, a simple sink move may only require opening part of the wall, while moving a toilet or shower often means cutting the slab to reroute the waste line and maintain proper slope. The work may also require new vent connections, patching concrete, and rebuilding tile or flooring after inspection. Homeowners should expect the slab to be opened only where the new pipe route needs to pass, not necessarily the entire bathroom. The biggest cost drivers are access, distance, and how much of the finished floor must be removed and restored. A contractor should verify pipe depth, structural constraints, and whether the new layout can tie into existing drains without creating drainage problems. If the goal is to avoid major demolition, the best strategy is often to keep wet fixtures close to their original positions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but only by cutting the slab in the areas needed for new drain and vent runs. Small relocations may be possible with limited demolition, while larger layout changes usually require breaking concrete, trenching, and restoring the slab before finishes go back in.
